Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council

  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  March 13, 2023
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:09 p.m., on Monday, March 13, 2023, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia,
Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Public Works/
Utilities Ray, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Library LohGuan, Director of
Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Police Chief Fraser, Director of Human Resources
Ko, Deputy Director Parks and Recreation Houghton

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Andrade-Stadler

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  PROCLAMATIONS – F2M23-3

  A.  Ratified the action of Mayor Andrade-Stadler in proclaiming the month of March, 2023
  as WOMEN’S HISTORY MONTH in Alhambra.

  B.  Ratified the action of Mayor Andrade-Stadler in proclaiming March, 2023 as RED
  CROSS MONTH in Alhambra. Mayor Andrade-Stadler presented the Red Cross
  Month proclamation to Patty Madera, Interim Executive Director - Greater San
  Gabriel and Pomona Valleys American Red Cross.

2.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: SENIOR SERVICES SUPERVISOR KATHY SPRECHER –
  F2M23-3

  Mayor Andrade-Stadler and the City Council commended and thanked Senior Services
  Supervisor Kathy Sprecher for her 18 years of faithful and loyal service to the Parks &
  Recreation Department and the City of Alhambra. Mayor Andrade-Stadler presented a
  Certificate of Service plaque to Ms. Sprecher for her outstanding work for the City.

  1
3-13-23
 3.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: PLANNING COMMISSIONER RON SAHU – F2M23-3, F2M22-
  34

  The City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, recognized the City’s former Planning
  Commissioner Ron Sahu, who recently stepped down from his position, for his four years of
  dedicated service to the City of Alhambra. Mayor Andrade-Stadler presented the Certificate of
  Service to Mr. Sahu.

PRESENTATIONS

4.  CHAMBER OF COMMERCE UPDATE – F2M21-43

  Alhambra Chamber of Commerce President, Mr. John Bwarie, presented an update for
  Chamber of Commerce activities from October 2022 to February 2023.

  Public Comment:

  1) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom, inquired about the total operating budget for Chamber
  activities, where the Chamber gets the bulk of their income, what percentage of their
  income is taxpayer dollars, requested access to the weekly updates provided from the
  Chamber to the City, and inquired about the costs for Chamber of Commerce services
  listed in their agreement with the City.

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ thanked Mr. BWARIE for his update, complimented
  the Chamber’s efforts on the Lunar New Year event, and inquired about the Chamber’s efforts
  to fill chronic business vacancies in the City. Mr. BWARIE responded to questions.

  Councilmember MALONEY reiterated how well the Lunar New Year event went, expressed
  appreciation for the Chamber’s efforts for highlighting businesses in the community.

  Vice Mayor MAZA inquired if there was a list of property owners that the Chamber uses for
  outreach. Mr. BWARIE responded to questions.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the Strategic Plan goals of attracting and retaining businesses
  and welcomed feedback from the Chamber to achieve those goals.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the City’s current zoning code update and inquired if
  the Chamber has been involved in that process. Mr. BWARIE responded to questions.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and order filed this informational report.

5.  CITY COUNCIL SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE REGARDING DEVELOPMENT OF THE
  BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN TRANSPORTATION IMPROVEMENT PLAN – F2M22-33,

  Councilmember PÉREZ and Councilmember MALONEY provided an update. On February
  28, 2023, Bicycle and Pedestrian Transportation Improvement Plan Subcommittee Members,
  Jeff Maloney and Sasha Renée Pérez, met with City staff and the City’s consultant on the
  Plan, Alta Planning + Design, to receive an update on the Plan’s development. Over the last
  several months Alta Planning + Design collected traffic and collision information and engaged
  the community on existing bicycle and pedestrian needs and concerns. As a result of this
  outreach work, which included surveys, site walks, bike and walk audits, an interactive map,
  virtual workshops, pop-up information booths at schools, parks, and the Joslyn Center, and a
  meeting with the Transportation Commission on March 8, 2023, Alta Planning + Design will

  2
3-13-23
   now move into data analysis to develop the City’s bicycle plan network and bicycle/pedestrian
  recommendations/enhancements. This evening, the Council Subcommittee Members will
  report on the Plan’s progress. Once Alta Planning + Design completes the analysis and
  provides a Draft Plan, the community will be invited to provide additional feedback on the Draft
  Plan before its final adoption.

  Public Comment:  None

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE noted that she was impressed with the proposed
  crosswalks, inquired about the outreach of the project, discussed the upcoming zoning code
  update and the potential impacts on this plan. Councilmember PÉREZ responded to questions.

  Councilmember MALONEY noted that the consultant of the project is aware of the pending
  housing element update and zoning code update.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER noted the importance of Alhambra becoming a pedestrian safe
  and bicycle friendly city.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and order filed this informational report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6-18)

All other items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 7, 9, 14, 15, and 16
were considered by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

6.  NIB: MAIN STREET, FOURTH STREET, AND MISSION ROAD SEWER MAIN
  REPLACEMENT PROJECT - PHASE 1 – F2M22-53, N2M23-31

  On December 12, 2022, the City Council rejected the bids received for the Main Street, Fourth
  Street, and Mission Road Sewer Main Replacement Project due to the bids being higher than
  the amount of funds available. Staff worked with the Design Engineers to reduce the scope of
  the project and now recommends the project be re-advertised in two phases. The first phase
  will be on Mission Road (from Fourth Street to Garfield Avenue) and Fourth Street (from
  Mission Road to Commonwealth Avenue). Phase 1 of the Project will replace approximately
  3,350 feet of existing 8-inch - 12-inch sewer main to 18-inch -21-inch sewer main. Plans and
  specifications have been prepared. Staff has reviewed the plans and found them to be
  consistent with the City’s standards.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Main Street, Fourth Street, and Mission Road Sewer Main
  Replacement Project – Phase 1 with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on March 30, 2023,
  and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AUTHORIZE RFP: DEVELOPMENT OF A FEASIBILITY STUDY FOR THE STORY PARK
  STORMWATER CAPTURE PROJECT – F2M23-29, RFP2M23-7

  3
3-13-23
   Director of Public Works RAY delivered a staff report. The City developed a Stormwater Master
  Plan in order to comply with the Safe Clean Water Program’s stringent funding requirements
  by implementing a cost-effective strategy to identify potential opportunities for stormwater
  projects and prioritize the planning process. The proposed Story Park site is identified as a
  priority concept in the Stormwater Master Plan. This project seeks to improve water quality
  from runoff discharged to the Upper LA River Watershed Area infiltration, and filtration
  features. The project is envisioned as a diversion, storage, infiltration, and filtration facility with
  the potential to offer runoff storage and water quality benefits for the jurisdictions of Alhambra,
  South Pasadena, San Marino, and Pasadena. The Safe Clean Water Program requires a
  feasibility study in order to compete for funding from the Regional Program for stormwater
  project design, construction, operations and maintenance, and other related eligible activities.

  Public Comment:  None

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY inquired what happens to the water when it’s
  captured in the retention basin underground. Director of Public Works RAY responded to
  questions.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals to
  qualified firms for the development of a feasibility study for the Story Park Stormwater Capture
  Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON HALSTEAD CIRCLE, HIDALGO AVENUE,
  AND MAIN STREET – F2M23-30, RFP2M23-8

  The Utilities Department regularly installs water mains to replace aging pipelines and to
  improve system reliability and water quality. The six-inch cast iron water main pipes on
  Halstead Circle between North and South Vega Street and on Hidalgo Avenue between Main
  Street and Alhambra Road were installed in the 1920’s. The four-inch cast iron water main
  pipe on Main Street between Champion Place and Hidalgo Avenue was installed in 1910. The
  water main pipes have a history of breaks. These water main lines should be replaced to
  improve flow and firefighting capabilities in an emergency. This project would replace the
  existing four-inch and six-inch cast iron water mains with new 8-inch ductile iron water mains.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  Professional Engineering Design Services for the Water Main Replacement Project on
  Halstead Circle, Hidalgo Avenue, and Main Street with proposals due no later than 4:00 p.m.
  on April 13, 2022; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  4
3-13-23
 9.  AWARD CONTRACT: DESIGN SERVICES FOR ACTIVE TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM
  (ATP) CROSSWALK TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES – F2M22-56, RFP2M22-18, C2M23-6,
  M2M23-11

  Director of Public Works RAY delivered a staff report. The Alhambra Active Transportation
  Program (ATP), Lit Crosswalk Traffic Control Devices, SGV Measure M Subregional funding
  consists of improvements at the following locations: Main St./Meridian Ave.; Valley
  Blvd./Monterey St.; Main St./Marguerita Ave.; Chapel Ave./ Elgin St.; Main St./Curtis Ave.;
  Valley Blvd./Date Ave.; Main St./Vega St.; Main St./Olive Ave.; and, Valley Blvd./Primrose Ave.
  The project design includes installation of pedestrian push button signals and signage at nine
  intersections that have an uncontrolled crosswalk. Pedestrian crossing control equipment at
  all nine intersections may include flashing beacons (standard beacons per CA-MUTCD or
  Rapid Rectangular Flashing Beacons) or in-road flashing lights along crosswalk lines. Staff
  circulated a Request for Proposals (RFP) for engineering design services for the completion
  of Plans-Specifications and Cost Estimates and received proposals from three companies.
  Staff reviewed and evaluated the responding proposals and found the proposal submitted by
  Stantec Consulting Services Inc. conforms to the RFP and received the highest rating. Staff
  shared the proposed Project with Alta Planning + Design Inc., the design team working on the
  City’s Bicycle and Pedestrian Transportation Plan, and they support the proposed
  improvements at uncontrolled crosswalks.

  Public Comment:  None

  Discussion: Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER inquired if Alta Planning + Design have been
  involved in the project. Director of Public Works RAY provided clarification.

  Action Taken: City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by the City
  Manager and City Attorney, to Stantec Consulting Services, Inc. in the amount of $94,796 for
  design service for the ATP Crosswalk Traffic Control Devices Project; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-11)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  NIB: REPLACEMENT OF ALHAMBRA POOLS MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT – F2M23-31,
  N2M23-32

  Alhambra Pools have heaters, chemical controllers, filters, chlorine tanks, pumps and other
  pool equipment that are reaching the end of their useful life. A fully operational swimming pool
  mechanical system is a necessity for Alhambra and Granada Park pools. Specifications and
  bid documentation have been completed for the Alhambra Pools Mechanical Equipment
  Replacement Project. The project will be funded with American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)
  funds. The project bids are due no later than 10:30 a.m. on March 30, 2023, in the office of the
  City Clerk and will be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors for the Alhambra Pools Mechanical Equipment Replacement Project;
  and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

3-13-23
   Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  AUTHORIZE RFP: LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICES FOR VARIOUS CITY
  PROPERTIES – F2M23-32, RFP2M23-6

  The City of Alhambra currently contracts with Parkwood Landscape Maintenance, Inc. for
  landscape maintenance services. The contract expires on June 30, 2023. Therefore, staff is
  requesting authorization from the City Council to circulate a Request for Proposals (RFP) for
  Landscape Maintenance Services for various City properties. Proposals will be due to the
  Parks & Recreation Department in City Hall by 4:30 p.m. on April 11, 2023.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Request for Proposals to
  prospective contractors to provide landscape maintenance services for various city properties,
  with proposals due by 4:30 p.m. on April 11, 2023; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

12.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: PURCHASE OF SHADE STRUCTURES FOR ALHAMBRA
  AND GRANADA PARK POOLS – F2M22-6B, C2M22-10, M2M23-34

  On March 14, 2022, the City Council awarded a contract to Pacific Play Systems Inc. for the
  Alhambra Pools Shade Structure Project in the amount of $249,500.00. There were two
  change orders totaling $24,009.25 for the project for additional drilling due to finding water
  lines and to move one shade from Granada Pool to Alhambra Pool due to finding unforeseen
  concrete in the excavation process. The total amount of the contract is $273.509.25. This
  project has been inspected by staff, and all work has been completed in accordance with the
  City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it would be appropriate for the City Council to
  accept this project as complete.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Pacific Play Systems Inc. for the
  Alhambra Pools Shade Structure Project as complete in the amount of $273,509.25; directed
  the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation;
  instructed the Finance Director to release the 5 percent retention 35 days from the date of
  recordation if no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M23-34)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  6
3-13-23
 13.  APPROVAL TO CANCEL MOTOROLA RIPA MODULE PURCHASE – F2M18-6B, C2M18-
  66, M2M23-35

  On December 13, 2018, the City entered into a contract for the purchase of public safety
  Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management System (RMS) for a total amount
  of $1,127,388.85 under a five-year lease. On June 27, 2022, the City Council approved a
  Motorola RIPA module agreement with an initial cost of $22,743 with an annual maintenance
  of $3,300. Since Council’s approval of the Motorola RIPA module, staff has not implemented
  the RIPA module due to Motorola’s inability to deliver the product. Motorola’s contract states
  staff can cancel the contract after giving 30 days’ notice of default and their failure to cure
  within 30 days. Staff will seek a different vendor to collect perceived demographic, and other
  detailed data regarding pedestrian and traffic stops and report to the California Department of
  Justice in compliance with AB 953 RIPA legislation.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the cancellation of Motorola’s RIPA module
  purchase agreement approved by the City Council on June 27, 2022; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-35)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  AUTHORIZE RFP: DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION AND DECORATION OF THE 2025-2029
  TOURNAMENT OF ROSES PARADE FLOATS – F2M23-33, RFP2M23-9

  Annually, the City conducts an art drawing contest that includes all elementary school students
  that attend school in the City of Alhambra. The winning art will be used each year to inspire
  the 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028, and 2029 Tournament of Roses Floats. After the winning art has
  been chosen, the City will seek a professional float builder to provide all services required to
  be an eligible Rose Parade Float entry. Elements shall include but are not limited to the
  concept, design, construction and floral decorating. Therefore, staff requests City Council
  authorization to circulate a Request for Proposals to provide Rose Parade Float design and
  build services for the 2025-2029 Tournament of Roses Parades. Proposals will be due to the
  Parks & Recreation Department in City Hall by 4:00 p.m. on April 13, 2023.

  Public Comment:

  1) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom, expressed concern that no amount is listed under the
  fiscal impact of the report, inquired about the benefits of Alhambra having a float in the
  Rose Parade, and expressed concern with the proposed 5-year term of a future contract
  with the chosen vendor.

  City Manager BINNQUIST responded to Ms. MICHELSON’s questions.

  Discussion: City Attorney MONTES noted that the years referenced in the staff report
  should be 2024-2028 instead of 2025-2029.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the importance of the City continuing to provide a float
  in the Rose Parade and noted it’s a long-standing tradition.

  7
3-13-23
   Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Request for Proposals to
  prospective contractors to provide Tournament of Roses Float design and build services for
  the 2025-2029 Tournament of Roses Parades, with proposals due by 4:00 pm on April 13,
  2023; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

15.  APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT AMENDMENT WITH CONSOLIDATED DISPOSAL
  SERVICES, L.L.C. DBA REPUBLIC SERVICES FOR REINSTATEMENT OF WEEKLY
  BULKY ITEM SWEEP SERVICE PROGRAM – F2M20-39, C2M21-9, M2M23-36

  Deputy City Manager STOVER and Recycling Specialist EIGIRDAS delivered a staff report.
  On February 22, 2021, the City of Alhambra (“the City”) entered into contract with Republic
  Services for residential and commercial integrated solid waste management services. The
  contract grants four courtesy bulky item pickups per year for residential customers and one
  courtesy bulky item pickup per unit per year for multi-family complex customers, upon
  scheduling such service. The prior contract included “weekly sweep” services on each area’s
  normal trash pick-up day for bulky items. Despite outreach efforts on the new bulky item
  collection policy and requirements for scheduled pick-ups, illegal dumping continues to be a
  frequent complaint throughout the City. Illegal dumping deteriorates the overall quality and
  appearance of the City’s neighborhoods and endangers the health and wellbeing of residents
  and pedestrians. The service reinstatement under the proposed Amendment will allow the
  “weekly sweep” of bulky items included in the City’s waste hauling contracts prior to the current
  2021 contract; therefore, restoring prior level of service. To account for costs associated under
  the proposed Amendment, an increase to residential and commercial account rates will result
  as described in the March 13, 2023 staff report by the Deputy City Manager and Recycling
  Assistant. If approved, the service reinstatement and change in monthly rates would
  commence April 1, 2023 to align with the residential quarterly bill cycle. All other provisions of
  the City’s contract with Republic will remain unchanged.

  Public Comment:

  1) Melody WU, via Zoom, suggested that the City provide education to the residents
  regarding dumping, noted that additional rates costs be a temporary solution, and
  encouraged higher fines for illegal dumping.

  2) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom, encouraged the Council to vote no on this item,
  encouraged additional education from the City on the four bulky item pickups already
  included for residential customers, expressed concern with the rate increase to residents,
  and encouraged the use of smaller bins for lower rate prices.

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ discussed the recent increase of illegal dumping in
  the City and inquired how the truck would be sent out to pick up illegal dumping. Deputy City
  Manager STOVER responded to questions.

  Councilmember MALONEY noted that this item is primarily to address the amount of illegal
  dumping in the City and inquired if piles of miscellaneous trash would be included under this
  contract amendment as well. Mitchell KOPCZYK, Republic Services, responded to questions.

  Councilmember MALONEY inquired about the length of the contract and if it would align with
  the original term of the agreement. Deputy City Manager STOVER responded to questions.

  8
3-13-23
   Councilmember LEE expressed concern with potential traffic congestion with an additional
  truck in the community picking up trash, inquired about the amount of bulky item pickups for
  multi-family complex and Deputy City Manager STOVER responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor MAZA thanked staff and republic services for putting this together and noted that
  this is an effort tot keep the City clean, inquired about the annual rate increase under the
  contract, and Mr. KOPCZYK responded to questions.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER expressed support for the item and supported the idea of making
  a phone number readily available to the community so they could call-in illegal dumping.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an Amendment, subject to review and approval
  by the City Manager and the City Attorney, to Contract No. C2M21-9 between the City of
  Alhambra and Consolidated Disposal Service, LLC dba Republic Services, for the
  reimplementation of a citywide “weekly sweep” service of bulky items at an additional
  residential and commercial rate cost; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize the Council’s action. (M2M23-36)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

16.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH CALTRANS
  FOR THE FREMONT RAMP AND INTERCHANGE IMPROVEMENTS – F2M19-32, C2M23-
  13, M2M23-37

  City Manager BINNQUIST delivered a staff report. “Advancing Alhambra” is the City’s plan to
  improve local roads and safety for residents and reduce traffic and congestion in Alhambra via
  various mobility improvements. To find solutions to Alhambra’s traffic and congestion
  concerns, the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) reallocated
  the transportation funds (Measure R) once approved for the 710 Tunnel Project to area
  municipalities to enhance transportation operations and address the congestion issues being
  experienced. Pursuant to this direction, the City of Alhambra conducted traffic studies in 2020
  and scoping in 2021 to help identify locations for mobility improvement consideration. Among
  the City’s options, four major ramp locations emerged as targets including Fremont, Atlantic,
  Garfield and the conversion of the 710 Stub at Valley into a four-lane arterial. Improvements
  at these locations are projected to help keep motorists on the I-10 rather than cutting through
  Alhambra, providing not only relief to the local community, but also not negatively altering
  regional traffic patterns. On March 2, 2023, the City received from Caltrans a Cooperative
  Agreement, which establishes the responsibilities of each agency in the preparation of the
  Project Approval and Environmental Document (PA&ED), Plans, Specifications, and
  Estimates (PS&E) and Right of Way (ROW). Elements of the Fremont Project include the ramp
  improvements on I-10 and a braided ramp between Northbound I-710 to Eastbound I-10
  Connector and Eastbound Fremont Interchange offramp. This Cooperative Agreement
  between the City and Caltrans does not finalize the City’s project at Fremont and the
  interchange; rather, it defines the responsibilities between Caltrans and the City with regard to
  continuing to process the project, including outreach, environmental review, design and
  ultimately, construction.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized entering into a Cooperative Agreement,
  subject to final language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the
  9
3-13-23
   City of Alhambra and the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) to complete the
  PA&ED, PS&E, and ROW for the Fremont Ramp and Interchange Improvements; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-37)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE
